subject: Complex numbers
title: Checking the Field Laws
subtitle: Every rule of arithmetic, proved for pairs; the one fact about real numbers that makes division possible; and why no number system of three dimensions can exist.
prerequisite_note: Chapter 4. Sections 5.8 to 5.10 use determinants and eigenvalues of small matrices, explained where they appear.
objectives: State the field laws and prove every one for the ordered pairs, including existence and uniqueness of inverses.
Prove the multiplication laws a second way through the matrix model M(z).
Decide for any field K whether pairs over K form a field: exactly when -1 is not a square in K.
Derive cancellation, the absence of zero divisors and the count of square roots from the field laws.
Prove that C is the only field of dimension 2 over R, with exactly two isomorphisms fixing R.
Prove that no field, and no real algebra without zero divisors, has odd dimension above 1 over R.
Define the quaternions, prove they form a division ring, and connect unit quaternions to single-qubit gates.

theorems.statement: M respects sums and products and is one-to-one; associativity follows
every non-zero pair has exactly one inverse; C is a field
pairs over a field K form a field iff -1 is not a square in K
consequences of the field laws: 0x = 0, no zero divisors, cancellation, (-1)x = -x, unique solutions, x^2 = y^2 iff x = +-y
a field of dimension 2 over R is isomorphic to C, with exactly two isomorphisms fixing R
a field of finite odd dimension over R is R
a real algebra with identity and no zero divisors of odd finite dimension has dimension 1
assuming the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra, every finite-dimensional field extension of R is R or C

quantum_links: Unit quaternions are SU(2); i, j, k are -iX, -iY, -iZ; unit quaternions give rotation gates R_n(theta).
reviewer_type: AI review with automated symbolic and numerical checks; no human mathematician review yet
